world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Jones, Ross McCallum 1998. The Boko/Busa Language Cluster (LINCOM); Wedekind 1972/73 Outline of the grammar of Busa — not readable online

new_statements.quote: Anmerkung. Die Busasprache hat die Tendenz, den dynamischen Ton bei Einzelnennung von Nomina auf die letzte Silbe bzw. den Schlußvokal zu legen. Infolgedessen figurieren bei den Gruppierungen die meisten Wörter mit langem und hochtonigem Vokal am Ende. Ich nehme an, daß dies von einem verlorengegangenen Artikel herrührt, habe aber noch keine bestimmten Anhaltspunkte dafür gefunden.
new_statements.translation: Note. The Busa language has the tendency to place the dynamic accent [stress], when nouns are named in isolation, on the last syllable, i.e. on the final vowel. As a result, in the groupings most words appear with a long, high-toned vowel at the end. I assume that this derives from a lost article, but have not yet found any definite evidence for it.
new_statements.citation: Funke, E[mil]. 1915. Die Sprache von Busa am Niger. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen an der Königlichen Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität zu Berlin 18, Abt. III (Afrikanische Studien): 52-84.
new_statements.locator: p. 58, section 'Abgeleitete Substantive', 'Anmerkung' between sub-sections e) and f) (= PDF p. 570 of the archive.org volume scan mitteilungen18berluoft)
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: 58; extracted text hits at lines 117077-117091). The volume title page (PDF p. 5) reads 'Mitteilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen... Jahrgang XVIII, Berlin 1915', so the citation MSOS 18 (1915): 52-84 is right (Glottolog's duplicate entry 74148 'vol. 16, 1913' is the erroneous one). QUOTE: the 'Anmerkung' between sub-sections e) and f) of 'Abgeleitete Substantive' on p. 58 reads exactly as quoted; the only difference is the line-break hyphenation 'Schluss-/vokal', joined in the transcription. READING: I read the surrounding section and pp. 52-56. p. 53 calls the language a 'echte Sudansprache' with 'musikalischen Silbenton'; pp. 55-56 'Der Ton' gives three level tones (hoch, mi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In a tone language (three level tones plus two contours, pp. 55-56), the dynamic (intensity) accent of nouns pronounced in isolation tends to fall on the last syllable / final vowel, which is then realised long and high-toned; Funke treats it as a tendency and suspects a historical (lost article) cause.
new_statements.exceptions: Framed as a 'Tendenz' (tendency), not an exceptionless rule; stated for nouns only and for citation forms ('Einzelnennung'); Funke himself suggests the final prominence may be a relic of a lost article rather than a stress rule proper. The rest of the sketch describes tone (pp. 55-56) and says nothing further about stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, nouns in citation (isolation) form; data from a single Hausa-speaking informant from the town of Busa (Bussa) on the Niger, elicited in Lomé (Togo) in early 1912 and cut short (pp. 52-53). Old primary source; the modern descriptions (Wedekind 1972/73, Jones 1998) were not accessible and may supersede it.
new_statements.identity_note: Funke 1915 describes the speech of one informant from the town of Busa (Bussa) on the Niger (old Bussa, whose population was moved to New Bussa in 1968), i.e. Busa proper busa1253 (New Busa/Wawa area), not the Illo dialect (illo1238) and not Bokobaru (boko1267) or Boko (boko1265). Glottolog's busa1253 bibliography is contaminated with Bisa [bib] (Burkina Faso) references (Vanhoudt, Prost 1950, Naden, Zouré, Vossen & Schreiber, Obeng), which describe a different Eastern Mande language.

sources.note: p. 58 note: the language tends to put the 'dynamischer Ton' (dynamic accent = stress) of nouns named in isolation on the last syllable / final vowel, so most words appear with a long high-toned final vowel; Funke suspects a lost article. pp. 55-56 'Der Ton': 3 level + 2 contour tones; nothing else on stress in the sketch.
